assessment: The study supports the existence of a new pathway for the removal of an important DNA lesion, 3meC in single stranded DNA during replication, that seems essential in yeast, but likely contributes in other organisms, and helps clarify the distinctive role of homologous recombination in DSB repair and post-replicative repair. The paper is of interest to an audience of DNA repair and cancer biologists because it seeks to refine the mechanism by which cells respond to DNA damage. This is an important topic, and the results are consistent with previous work in the field. New claims could change our understanding of DNA repair with implications for mutagenesis and cancer therapy.
